aiAgentFacts.fact: In a random sample of 22,333 UK dogs under primary veterinary care in 2016, the one-year period prevalence of diagnosed otitis externa was 7.30% (95% CI 6.97-7.65).
Breed and ear carriage were the highest-ranked risk factors for otitis externa in this cohort.
Pendulous ear carriage carried 1.76 times the odds (95% CI 1.48-2.10) and V-shaped drop ear carriage 1.84 times the odds (95% CI 1.53-2.21) of otitis externa versus erect ear carriage.

Highest-odds breeds versus crossbreds were Basset Hound (5.87), Chinese Shar Pei (3.44), Labradoodle (2.95), Beagle (2.54) and Golden Retriever (2.23); protected breeds were Chihuahua (0.20), Border Collie (0.34), Yorkshire Terrier (0.49) and Jack Russell Terrier (0.52).
Designer breed types overall had 1.63 times the odds (95% CI 1.31-2.03) of otitis externa compared with crossbred dogs.

All recurrent ear infections in dogs are secondary; good long-term outcomes require diagnosing the primary condition, treating secondary infection, correcting predisposing risks and reversing perpetuating factors.
Most ear canal surgery is considered avoidable if recurrent otitis is properly managed at an earlier stage.
Ear carriage was assigned at breed level rather than measured on individual dogs, so the conformation findings describe breed groups and not any individual animal's anatomy.

historyQuestions: Supported by the review's framework rather than prescribed by the cohort study: for any repeat presentation, establish the number and dates of previous episodes, which ear, what was prescribed, and whether each episode fully resolved — recurrence signals an undiagnosed primary condition.
redFlags: Not defined by either paper. Neither identifies urgency thresholds; pain on head handling is described as a clinical sign, not a triage criterion.
differentialDiagnosesMentioned: The review frames recurrent otitis using primary, secondary, predisposing and perpetuating factors — allergic skin disease is named in the cohort study as a common underlying tendency — but neither paper provides a differential list.
recommendedDiagnosticWorkups: Not evaluated by the cohort study. The review's position is that recurrent cases require identification of the primary condition rather than repeated topical courses; specific diagnostics are not prescribed here.

limitations: Prevalence counts diagnoses recorded in one year of clinical notes; unpresented or home-managed ear disease is invisible, so 7.30% is a floor
Breed odds may partly reflect differential examination and presentation rates rather than true incidence — a record-based design cannot separate the two
Ear carriage was classified at breed level, not measured on individual dogs, so within-breed anatomical variation is unaddressed
No severity distribution is reported: 'diagnosed with otitis externa' spans a single mild episode to chronic end-stage disease
No prevention or treatment was tested by the cohort study — ear cleaning, products, drying and plucking are all unevaluated, which is why its guidance is cautious rather than prescriptive
Nuttall 2023 is a narrative review, so its clinical framework carries expert-opinion weight rather than trial evidence
